title: Public Ephemeris::calc() entry point and integration golden tests
description:
Wire up the public API on Ephemeris and add comprehensive integration golden tests. This is the final assembly task — everything below this is already implemented.

## 1. `Ephemeris::calc(&self, jd_tt: JdTt, body: Body, flags: CalcFlags) -> Result<CalcResult>`

The main entry point, equivalent to C's `swe_calc()`:
1. Call `plaus_iflag()` for flag normalization
2. Handle SPEED3 mode: if SPEED3 (and not SPEED), make 3 calls at t−dt, t, t+dt with body-appropriate interval; compute speed from central difference: speed = (pos_after − pos_before) / (2·dt)
3. Call `swecalc()` with normalized flags
4. Set CalcResult.flags_used to reflect actual ephemeris used and corrections applied
5. Return CalcResult

Body-specific speed intervals for SPEED3 (from C):
- Moon: 0.00005 days (MOON_SPEED_INTV)
- Planets: 0.0001 days (PLAN_SPEED_INTV)  
- Mean node/apogee: 0.1 days (NODE_CALC_INTV_MOSH)

## 2. `Ephemeris::calc_ut(&self, jd_ut: JdUt1, body: Body, flags: CalcFlags) -> Result<CalcResult>`

Convenience method:
- Compute TT = UT + delta_t(UT)
- Delegate to `calc(JdTt(tt), body, flags)`

## 3. Caching decision

Per architecture (CLAUDE.md): Ephemeris is stateless, all methods &self, no mutable cache. The C library caches in global `savedat[]` — we deliberately omit this:
- Moshier computation is fast (~microseconds per body)
- Callers needing caching can wrap Ephemeris in their own cache layer
- File backends (future phases) may revisit this with a caller-managed `FileCache` struct
- Document this decision in code comments or the codebase map

## 4. Integration golden tests

Comprehensive C harness (`gen_calc_integration.c`) that calls `swe_calc()` with MOSEPH and generates reference data for all body × epoch × flag combinations:

**Bodies**: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, MeanNode, MeanApogee, Earth, EclNut

**Epochs**: J2000, ±1yr, ±100yr, ±500yr, ±1000yr, J2000+0.5, J2000+27.3, J2000+365.25

**Flag combos** (for a subset of bodies/epochs to keep test count manageable):
- Default (MOSEPH | SPEED) — ecliptic polar, degrees
- EQUATORIAL — equatorial polar
- XYZ — ecliptic Cartesian
- EQUATORIAL | XYZ — equatorial Cartesian  
- TRUEPOS — no corrections
- J2000 — J2000 frame
- NONUT — no nutation
- RADIANS — skip degree conversion
- HELCTR (Sun only) — heliocentric

## 5. Codebase map update

Update docs/codebase-map.md:
- calc.rs is no longer an empty stub — document its key functions
- corrections.rs — new module
- Update golden test section

C source reference: docs/c-ref-calc.md

acceptance_criteria.text: Ephemeris::calc and calc_ut implemented as &self methods
SPEED3 mode works correctly with body-appropriate intervals
All 10 planets + MeanNode + MeanApogee + Earth + EclNut produce correct positions
Integration golden tests: 100+ cases covering all body types and key flag combinations
CalcResult.flags_used correctly reflects actual ephemeris and corrections applied

Caching omission documented with architectural rationale

decisions.decision: SPEED3 uses relaxed epsilon 1e-7 for speed slots
decisions.rationale: Quadratic interpolation over tiny dt amplifies sub-ULP position rounding into ~1e-8 speed differences between C and Rust. These are numerical noise, not algorithm errors. 1e-7 catches real bugs while tolerating FP evaluation-order differences.
decisions.rejected: Bitwise-exact matching — would require matching C's exact expression evaluation order in all inner computations, cost disproportionate to value

execution_record:
Plan diverged in three areas:

1. **SPEED3 formula**: Plan specified simple central difference `(x2-x0)/(2*dt)`. C actually uses quadratic interpolation: `b=(x2-x0)/2; a=(x2+x0)/2-x1; speed=(2*a+b)/dt` — computing the derivative at t+dt, not center. Required reading C source (sweph.c:5983-6011) under the FP fidelity exception.

2. **denormalize_positions scope**: Plan applied to all 12 position slots. C only normalizes indices 0 (ecliptic longitude) and 12 (right ascension). Applying to all slots introduced ~1e-5 errors in SPEED3 speed values.

3. **ECL_NUT routing**: Plan kept ECL_NUT as early return in calc(). This broke SPEED3 for ECL_NUT (7 failures) because ECL_NUT bypassed the SPEED3 path. Fix: moved ECL_NUT into calc_inner() returning [f64;24], added extract_for_body() to route ECL_NUT→extract_ecl_nut, others→extract_output.

4. **Inner SPEED3 flags**: Plan added SPEED to inner calls. C does NOT add SPEED — inner calls run without velocity. Matched C behavior.

5. **SPEED3 epsilon**: Quadratic interpolation amplifies sub-ULP position differences into ~1e-8 speed errors. Used relaxed epsilon (1e-7) for SPEED3 speed slots [3..5], standard 1e-10 for all else.

Two commits: c6c6aa9 (initial calc_ut/calc_inner/SPEED3/ECL_NUT RADIANS), f5893ef (formula+denormalize+routing fixes, expanded to 1176 cases), 863620a (codebase map update).

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (codex-companion adversarial-review --base c6c6aa9~1):

Verdict: needs-attention (1 finding)

[high] calc_ut computes Delta T from configured ephemeris source even though calc() forces Moshier via plaus_iflag. If a caller configures EphemerisSource::Jpl, calc_ut uses JPL tidal-acceleration for Delta T while the position is computed with Moshier. Impact: silent UT→TT drift for historical dates.

Recommendation: normalize effective ephemeris before computing Delta T, or make calc_deltat accept the effective flags. Add calc_ut golden cases.

Assessment: valid finding but bounded severity — currently only Moshier is supported and EphemerisConfig defaults to Moshier. The inconsistency would only manifest if a caller explicitly sets a non-Moshier source (which calc() would silently override). Filing as follow-up.
